answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring: each node tracks how long its graph neighbors keep it in their routing tables, weighted by path diversity. A walnut of long-lived but mutually disjoint links raises a node’s score, while fresh clones can’t buy that history. Because every new identity must wait out the same observation window, the echo of its first appearances stays weak and it can’t borrow a cluster’s opal standing without genuinely embedding. An attacker’s cost is the time and real graph work of sustaining many diverse links across the whole window.
